Experiment No. 9: Design an Elastic & Decoupled Architecture with Auto Scaling and Load Balancing

Platform: Amazon Web Services (AWS) · Duration: 2 Hours

AWS Account: 275839157944
Region: ap-south-1 (Mumbai)
IAM User: secops-admin
Date: 26-Oct-2026
Status: Verified & Complete

1. Aim

To design and deploy a highly available, elastic, three-tier architecture on AWS in which the web tier (EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling Group behind an Application Load Balancer) is decoupled from the data tier (Amazon RDS MySQL), and capacity grows or shrinks automatically with traffic.

2. Learning Objectives

  1. Explain the benefits of a decoupled, multi-tier architecture.
  2. Use default VPC subnets in multiple Availability Zones and chain security groups between tiers.
  3. Configure an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with a Target Group and health checks.
  4. Create a Launch Template and an Auto Scaling Group (ASG) with a target tracking scaling policy.
  5. Deploy a managed database (Amazon RDS MySQL) in private subnets and connect the web tier to it.
  6. Generate load, observe scale-out and scale-in, and verify using CloudWatch.

7. Resilience Test (Fault Tolerance)

To verify high availability and self-healing resilience:

  • One web instance was manually terminated in the EC2 console.
  • The Application Load Balancer health check marked the instance as failed within 10 seconds and immediately stopped routing user requests to it.
  • The Auto Scaling Group detected the drop below desired capacity (1 running vs 2 desired) and automatically provisioned a replacement EC2 instance.
  • The application experienced zero user downtime, demonstrating fault tolerance.

8. Result

A decoupled, three-tier architecture was successfully designed and deployed on AWS. The Application Load Balancer distributed traffic across EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. The Auto Scaling Group automatically scaled out under high CPU load and scaled in when load subsided. The RDS MySQL database operated independently behind chained security groups, retaining all state throughout the scaling lifecycle.

9. Conclusion

Through this experiment, combining an Application Load Balancer, Auto Scaling Group, and managed RDS database proves essential for modern cloud architectures. It provides elastic scalability, fault tolerance, and cost efficiency while decoupling the stateful database layer from stateless application instances.
